title: US blockade and Hormuz shipping standoff continue
summary: The US keeps a naval blockade on Iranian ports. Iran restricts the Strait of Hormuz.
Ship traffic through the strait was about 65 percent below pre-war levels in the latest weekly UKMTO count.
Iran says tankers hit mines. Maritime officials have not confirmed this.
why_it_matters: A large share of world oil and gas normally passes the strait, so the standoff affects energy prices worldwide.
verify_note: Iranian claims of mine strikes on tankers are not independently confirmed. UKMTO reported a tanker fire on 7 November near Khasab, Oman, with no stated cause.

sources.title: How does Iran view Trump sidelining Vance from talks?
sources.supports: US blockade and sanctions continue. UKMTO counted 139 outbound and 169 inbound transits in a week, about 65 percent below pre-war. Eight incidents recorded.

sources.title: Iran downplays new U.S. task force aimed at disrupting ground transport routes
sources.supports: US blockade redirected 144 vessels through October. US forces disabled the cargo ship Huda on 7 November. Iran reported tankers hitting mines; officials did not confirm.

sources.title: Iran's calculations as US escalation looms: Trust, midterms, Hormuz
sources.supports: October attacks on shipping were the highest on record, per the Washington Institute. Iran says it reopens the strait only after the US takes concrete steps.

sources.title: Tanker Hit by Limpet Mines in Strait of Hormuz as New Threat to Shipping Emerges
sources.supports: UKMTO counted 145 conflict-related incidents since 28 February, 88 involving ships in the strait, through 28 October. Reuters could not verify the Guards' mine claims.

title: How the US-Iran war reached today's standoff
summary: The US and Israel struck Iran on 28 February 2026. Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei was killed.
A Pakistan-brokered ceasefire began in April. A June memorandum promised an end to fighting and talks toward a final deal.
Fighting resumed in July after ship attacks. Now there is neither full war nor peace.
why_it_matters: Every current question, from the blockade to the nuclear stock, comes from the war that began on 28 February and its failed deals.
verify_note: Sources differ by a day or so on some dates: ceasefire 7 or 8 April, memorandum announced 14 June and called the 17 June memorandum elsewhere. Signing was planned for 19 June, per France 24.

sources.title: US-Iran war, then and now: How the landscape has changed since February
sources.supports: Strikes began 28 February during nuclear talks. Khamenei was killed and his son Mojtaba succeeded him. Brent rose from $72 to a peak above $126.

sources.title: Pakistan army chief in Tehran: Can diplomacy prevent new US-Iran fighting?
sources.supports: Pakistan brokered the 8 April ceasefire. A 14-point June memorandum followed. Its 60-day window expired mid-August. Trump rejected an Iranian proposal on 26 September.

sources.title: March to July: What's different as US-Iran fighting escalates again?
sources.supports: Iran struck three vessels on 6 July and the US replied the next day. Trump called the ceasefire over and Iran shut the strait again.

sources.title: US and Iran agree to 'immediate' end of military operations in memorandum of understanding
sources.supports: Pakistan announced the memorandum on 14 June. It promised to reopen the strait, end the blockade, and start nuclear talks within about two months.

sources.title: Iran leader Khamenei killed in massive US and Israeli attack
sources.supports: Khamenei was killed in the opening wave of a large US and Israeli attack on 28 February. Iran fired at Israel and US Gulf bases.

sources.title: US-Iran ceasefire deal: What are the terms, and what's next?
sources.supports: A two-week Pakistan-brokered ceasefire followed about 40 days of US-Israeli attacks.

title: Small strikes and drone attacks keep flaring
summary: US officials called a 2 November US strike on Qeshm Island defensive.
Trump confirmed minor strikes on 6 November. Iranian state media said Qeshm was hit.
Iran's Guards say they struck a US radar in Bahrain on 13 November and sent six drones on 15 November. The US and Bahrain say they downed them.
why_it_matters: The Guards say they will respond "without limits" if attacks recur, and Trump says he is ready to return to war if talks fail.
verify_note: Claims are disputed. Al Jazeera says neither side's account of 13 November could be confirmed.

sources.title: US denies Iran's claim it hit two radar sites in Bahrain
sources.supports: The Guards say they destroyed a US radar in Bahrain. CENTCOM says it shot down two drones and no radar was hit. Neither side's claim could be confirmed.

sources.title: Bahrain says it intercepted Iranian attacks after Tehran claims it targeted U.S. assets
sources.supports: On 15 November the Guards said six drones targeted a US radar at Al-Riffa in Bahrain. Bahrain said it intercepted them.

sources.title: US hits Qeshm Island, Pezeshkian signals more diplomacy: Iran war latest
sources.supports: US forces struck Qeshm Island on 2 November, called defensive by US officials. A source described the strikes as limited, not a resumed major operation.

sources.title: Iran downplays new U.S. task force aimed at disrupting ground transport routes
sources.supports: Trump confirmed minor strikes on 6 November after reports of missiles hitting Qeshm. Iran claimed it downed another US drone there.

title: Iran's uranium stock unchecked as IAEA is blocked
summary: The IAEA has no access to bombed sites and cannot confirm where Iran's enriched uranium is.
The IAEA estimated about 440 kg of 60 percent enriched uranium before the June 2025 strikes. Nobody has verified it since.
Iran reportedly told the IAEA that inspections cannot resume while the US threatens attack.
why_it_matters: Without inspections nobody can verify whether Iran is rebuilding a weapons-capable programme, which is the US core demand.
verify_note: The 440 kg figure is the IAEA estimate from before the June 2025 strikes and is unverified since, per AFP. Reports of IAEA visits to Bushehr were seen only in a search summary and are not used.

sources.title: Bahrain says it intercepted Iranian attacks after Tehran claims it targeted U.S. assets
sources.supports: IAEA has no access to the Isfahan enrichment plant and does not know if it holds material. Iran says it will not remove enriched material from the country.

sources.title: Iran rules out nuclear inspections while under threat from US
sources.supports: Iran reportedly told the IAEA inspections cannot resume amid persistent public threats from the US president.

sources.title: IAEA calls for access to Iran nuclear sites over proliferation concerns
sources.supports: IAEA quarterly report calls the lack of access a proliferation concern. Iran's atomic chief said bombed sites need special inspection protocols.

sources.title: After six months of war, what have US, Iran gained and lost?
sources.supports: Iran is believed to hold about 440 kg of highly enriched uranium and refused US demands to hand it over or commit to zero enrichment.

sources.title: UN nuclear watchdog chief urges Iran to grant access
sources.supports: IAEA chief Grossi told the UN Security Council Iran must grant access. No IAEA access to key sites since June 2025; the 440 kg of 60 percent uranium is unverified.

title: Iran's oil exports halted by blockade, reports say
summary: Bloomberg reported on 19 October that no tankers had docked at Kharg Island's crude terminals since late August.
Tanker tracker Windward said Kharg loadings had already stopped by 31 July. Bloomberg says most exports went to China.
The US launched a sanctions push called Operation Economic Outcast in late August, Al Jazeera reports.
why_it_matters: The blockade cost Iran at least 6 billion dollars in oil revenue, Al Jazeera reported in August. China's refiners are seeking other supply, Bloomberg says.
verify_note: Current Kharg loadings rest on one Bloomberg report (19 October, carried by gCaptain). Windward dates the halt earlier, to 31 July. No November data was found.

sources.title: Iran's main oil terminals remain empty as US blockade bites
sources.supports: No tankers docked at Kharg crude terminals since late August. Exports fell from almost 1 million barrels a day in July to nothing. Chinese refiners sought other supply.

sources.title: After six months of war, what have US, Iran gained and lost?
sources.supports: The US naval blockade cut Iran's oil revenue by at least 6 billion dollars. China opposes sanctions on Iran but stays out of the fighting.

sources.title: US-Iran war, then and now: How the landscape has changed since February
sources.supports: The US launched Operation Economic Outcast in late August to penalise firms doing business with Iran. Brent was above 114 dollars that day.

sources.title: Kharg Standstill and a Russian Convoy on the Arctic Route
sources.supports: Satellite and tracking data show the Kharg terminals at a standstill, with zero departures from 31 July to 9 August under the renewed US blockade.

title: Mediated talks stall as Trump cools on a deal
summary: Iran lists seven conditions. Qatar's prime minister reportedly carried a two-day Iranian proposal to Washington.
On 9 November Trump said "Iran militarily is effectively over". By 12 to 13 November he said the US does not need a deal.
Trump told Vice President Vance to focus on domestic matters and said a deal is no longer a priority.
why_it_matters: With talks stuck, the blockade and Hormuz restrictions stay in place and renewed strikes remain possible.
verify_note: Iran's Rezaei calls reports of progress fake. Khaleej Times says senior US and Gulf officials doubt an imminent deal.

sources.title: After meeting Qatar PM, Trump calls Iran war 'effectively over' militarily
sources.supports: Trump met Qatar's prime minister and called the war effectively over. The Qatari PM reportedly carried a two-day Iranian proposal to end the war.

sources.title: How does Iran view Trump sidelining Vance from talks?
sources.supports: Trump told Vance to focus on domestic matters and said a deal is not a priority. Iran demands seven conditions and sequenced concessions. No breakthrough is expected.

sources.title: Pakistan army chief in Tehran: Can diplomacy prevent new US-Iran fighting?
sources.supports: Pakistan's army chief made his fifth Tehran visit since April. Qatar handles detailed proposals. Russia's Lavrov visited Tehran on 19 October.

sources.title: Bahrain says it intercepted Iranian attacks after Tehran claims it targeted U.S. assets
sources.supports: Trump said on 12 to 13 November the US does not need a deal. Iran says it will not negotiate until a formal ceasefire is in place.

sources.title: Trump says Qatar, UAE, other Gulf allies prefer 'status quo', to keep up Hormuz blockade
sources.supports: Trump keeps the Hormuz blockade and holds off new strikes for now. Senior US and Gulf officials doubt an imminent deal.

hotspot: Yemen, Saudi Arabia and the Red Sea
title: Houthis claim more strikes on Saudi Arabia
summary: Houthi forces took Yemen's Red Sea coast in September. ACLED found no corroborated attacks on ships since 24 August.
Since July they have declared a blockade of Saudi-linked shipping and fired drones and missiles at Saudi targets.
Saudi Arabia says it now sends about 4 million barrels a day through its Yanbu port.
why_it_matters: Saudi oil exports and Red Sea shipping are exposed while the Strait of Hormuz is already disrupted.
verify_note: The 12 November strikes rest on one wire (Reuters), carried by Al Jazeera and The Jerusalem Post. Saudi authorities have not confirmed the Houthi claim on Riyadh airport; the coalition reports intercepting drones. The ACLED report prints no date; 1 October is approximate.

sources.title: Yemen's Houthis renew strikes on Saudi Arabia as UNSC extends sanctions
sources.supports: Houthis claim new strikes on Saudi oil and air sites; Saudi coalition reports intercepts; UN Security Council extends Yemen sanctions and condemns the attacks; over 333,000 displaced since August.

sources.title: Houthi gains around Bab al-Mandab raise risks to Red Sea shipping and global oil markets
sources.supports: Houthis advanced about 150 km along the coast in September, announced a blockade of Saudi-linked shipping in July, and hit about 10 ships; no corroborated attacks since 24 August.

sources.title: Can the Houthis close the Red Sea after seizing the Yemen coast?
sources.supports: Houthis hold Yemen's whole Red Sea coast after taking Mocha; Saudi exports rely on the East-West pipeline; experts disagree on how long they can sustain a blockade.

sources.title: Inside Tehran talks: Iranians link Houthi de-escalation to US approval of regional truce
sources.supports: Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish officials met Iranian leaders; no deal. Iran says it lacks leverage over the Houthis, its main outside backer, and links calm to a US-approved regional truce.

sources.title: Houthi attacks prompt Saudi Yanbu warnings as missile intercepted near Medina
sources.supports: Saudi alerts for Yanbu; the coalition destroyed a Houthi missile heading toward Medina; Saudi authorities did not confirm the Houthi claim on Riyadh airport.

title: Gaza ceasefire stalls as Israeli strikes continue
summary: The truce began in October 2025, but Israeli strikes continue.
Israel holds about 60 percent of Gaza, according to Al Jazeera; other reports say about half.
The stabilisation force has not deployed. Israel and Hamas disagree on disarmament versus withdrawal.
why_it_matters: About 280,000 displaced people are in flood-risk sites or unsafe buildings ahead of winter, per a UN report cited by The Intercept.
verify_note: Death tolls come from Gaza's health ministry and cannot be independently checked. The 15 to 16 November strike rests on one CNN report, read through a republisher.

sources.title: Israel kills senior Hamas commander in Gaza two months after killing his predecessor as ceasefire stagnates
sources.supports: Israel says it killed Hamas's Rafah Brigade commander; over 1,600 killed since the truce per Gaza health officials; stabilisation force and committee absent; tents blocked at the border.

sources.title: What has Trump's Board of Peace achieved in a year since Gaza 'ceasefire'?
sources.supports: Israel holds about 60 percent of Gaza; about 227 aid trucks a day against a 600 target; stabilisation force not deployed; Hamas and Israel deadlocked on disarmament.

sources.title: Palestinians Are Trapped Between War and Peace With "Ceasefire"
sources.supports: Gaza ministry reports 74,494 killed in total as of 21 October; UN Resolution 2803 sets up the Board of Peace until end of 2027; flooding and unsafe shelter ahead of winter.

title: Israel holds south Lebanon as Hezbollah refuses disarmament
summary: Hezbollah fired on Israel in early March, citing the attacks on Iran, a US congressional report says.
Israel then launched a ground offensive. It still holds positions in the south despite a 26 June framework.
On 16 November Israel hit a reported Hezbollah arms shipment near the Syrian border.
why_it_matters: The standoff over who moves first, disarmament or withdrawal, blocks peace, and the UN force's mandate ends on 31 December.
verify_note: The claim of an arms shipment is Israel's; Lebanon's news agency reported no casualties or damage.

sources.title: Israel Strikes East Lebanon, Says Targeting Hezbollah Arms
sources.supports: Israel struck the Anti-Lebanon mountains saying it hit an arms shipment; Lebanese authorities have a disarmament plan Hezbollah rejects; US envoy Waltz visited.

sources.title: Lebanon, November 2026 Monthly Forecast
sources.supports: Israeli forces hold semi-permanent positions in the south; US-mediated talks in Florida on 20 to 21 October had no breakthrough; UNIFIL's mandate ends 31 December 2026.

sources.title: Israel continues attacks on Syria, Lebanon despite US push for diplomacy
sources.supports: Lebanon's health ministry says 4,350 killed and 12,310 wounded since 2 March; Israeli strikes and demolitions continued in the south.

sources.title: Lebanon: Background and U.S. Relations
sources.supports: Hezbollah resumed firing into Israel in early March 2026, citing the US and Israeli attacks on Iran; Israel launched a large ground offensive. The 26 June framework has not gone beyond two pilot zones.

sources.title: Waltz visits Beirut as UN peacekeepers set to leave with Lebanon and Israel still at odds
sources.supports: US ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz met Aoun, Salam and Berri on 16 November to discuss what replaces UNIFIL. Lebanon's presidency cites Israel's failure to comply with the framework.

title: Iraq's PM orders army into Kataib Hezbollah area
summary: On 16 November PM Ali al-Zaidi ordered the army into Jurf al-Sakhar, a Kataib Hezbollah area, AFP reports.
It followed a probe into oil smuggling there. Kataib Hezbollah calls it blackmail and refuses to disarm.
The US-led coalition ended its mission in Iraq on 30 September, The National reports.
why_it_matters: A clash between the army and a strong Iran-aligned militia could destabilise Iraq.
verify_note: AFP (16 November), The National (11 November) and FDD's Long War Journal (10 November) report the confrontation. FDD is an advocacy think tank. Whether the army has entered was not known on 17 November.

sources.title: Iraq Orders Army to Enter Jurf al-Sakhar as Confrontation with Kataib Hezbollah Escalates
sources.supports: Zaidi ordered the armed forces into Jurf al-Sakhar on 16 November, with a deadline (Friday, per a security source) for the faction to leave. Nine officials were dismissed after a probe confirmed oil smuggling. Kataib Hezbollah calls it blackmail.

sources.title: Iraqi PM orders inquiry into oil product smuggling in area controlled by Iran-backed militia
sources.supports: Zaidi ordered a probe in Jurf al-Sakhar; disarmament plan pushed to 30 June 2027; Kataib Hezbollah and Nujaba refuse while other factions agree.

sources.title: Kataib Hezbollah sets conditions on Iraq weapons talks
sources.supports: Kataib Hezbollah demanded full US withdrawal and other conditions for any weapons deal; Quds Force commander reportedly urged factions not to disarm.

sources.title: 'Resistance has won this round:' Kataib Hezbollah denies disarmament deal after US troops leave Iraq
sources.supports: US-led coalition forces withdrew from Iraq on 30 September. Kataib Hezbollah denies any disarmament deal with Zaidi and says its weapons stay with its fighters.

sources.title: Attack targets Khor Mor gas field in Iraqi Kurdistan
sources.supports: Zaidi's push against Iran-aligned factions' economic networks has led to an escalating confrontation with Kataib Hezbollah. He set a June 2027 deadline for weapons under state control.

title: Syria and Saudi Arabia sign defence cooperation deal
summary: Syria's and Saudi Arabia's defence ministries signed a cooperation deal on 4 November, during President al-Sharaa's visit to Riyadh.
Terms were not published. Saudi Arabia also pledged over $403 million in loans for rebuilding.
Syria says it is weighing joining the Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani defence pact. Its membership is not agreed.
why_it_matters: Syria's new government is aligning with Saudi Arabia as Riyadh looks for support against Houthi attacks.
verify_note: No Syrian deployment announced. Syria-Israel contacts: US-mediated talks took place in August; no later reporting was opened, so that thread is not included.

sources.title: Syria, Saudi Arabia sign defence cooperation deal, agree $403m in loans
sources.supports: Defence ministries signed an agreement with undisclosed terms; six Saudi loans worth over $403m; leaders called for safe Red Sea, Bab al-Mandeb and Hormuz routes.

sources.title: Syria, Saudi Arabia expand partnership with defense cooperation agreement amid Houthi threat
sources.supports: Neither side disclosed terms; Syria's foreign minister says it is exploring the Mecca joint defence pact; Turkey's parliament approved it 279 to 119; no deployments announced.

sources.title: Saudi, Syrian defence ministries sign cooperation agreement
sources.supports: Reuters: the defence ministries signed during Sharaa's visit; no terms disclosed; six Saudi Fund for Development loans worth over $403 million.

title: Ukraine hits Crimean bridge again amid record drone raids
summary: Ukraine struck the Crimean bridge for a second night on 17 November. Moscow-appointed officials say traffic was suspended.
Russia's defence ministry says it downed a record 1,441 Ukrainian drones. Russia hit Kyiv's two main bridges.
Talks in Abu Dhabi on 10 and 11 November agreed a prisoner swap, not territory.
why_it_matters: Strikes on refineries and power networks hit energy supply, and talks have not moved the two sides closer on land or security.
verify_note: The drone totals come from Russia's defence ministry and the damage claims from Ukraine and the bridge maker Fire Point; neither is independently confirmed.

sources.title: Ukraine attacks Crimean bridge for 2nd consecutive night
Ukraine Strikes Crimean Bridge for Second Day as Russia Pounds Kyiv Bridges
Ukraine launches biggest drone attack on Russia since war began
sources.supports: Russia's defence ministry says 1,336 Ukrainian drones were downed; a Crimea bridge and refineries were hit; Abu Dhabi talks brought a prisoner swap deal but no progress on territory.

sources.title: Russia and Ukraine hold nearly 4 hours of U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi
sources.supports: First US-mediated talks in nine months; Russia wants Ukraine out of four annexed regions, Ukraine wants a ceasefire and rejects ceding land; fighting continued during talks.

sources.publisher: Institute for the Study of War (via Kyiv Post)
sources.title: ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, November 15, 2026
sources.supports: ISW says Ukraine advanced south of Novopavlivka, Russia is striking Ukrainian energy sites, and Estonia will close its border with Russia after an alleged arson attempt.

sources.title: US to mediate trilateral talks with Ukraine, Russia in Abu Dhabi next week, US envoy says
sources.supports: US envoy Steve Witkoff announced the 10 to 11 November talks; the US also planned security guarantee talks with European allies in Brussels.

title: China holds unannounced drills around Taiwan
summary: Taiwan says China massed more than 100 military and coast guard ships in early November.
Beijing gave no name or advance notice. Taiwan calls it intimidation.
Activity fell by 8 to 9 November; about 70 ships were still in the first island chain on 13 November.
why_it_matters: Large drills near Taiwan raise the risk of an incident, days before Trump is expected to meet Xi at the APEC summit in Shenzhen.
verify_note: Reuters and France 24 opened. Numbers come from Taiwan's officials; China's defence ministry did not comment. The Reuters 10 November report is the same wire as the 13 November one. A Reuters detail about a submarine missile test was left out as single-sourced.

sources.title: China stages unannounced Pacific drills in intimidation of Taiwan
sources.supports: Taiwan officials say over 100 vessels massed; Taiwan's defence ministry calls it area denial; Xi's speech urged peaceful reunification and did not mention force.

sources.title: What we know about China's military exercises around Taiwan
sources.supports: Drills began in early November without advance notice; 49 aircraft on 3 November, one on 8 to 9 November; an analyst says they may be winding down.

sources.title: Taiwan says China is conducting 'area denial' drills in Western Pacific
sources.supports: Taiwan says more than 100 naval and coast guard ships are holding area denial drills, ahead of the APEC summit in Shenzhen.

title: Pakistan and Taliban trade fire on border
summary: Pakistani and Afghan Taliban forces clashed along the border on 29 October and again on 1 November.
Pakistan accuses the Taliban of sheltering the Pakistani Taliban (TTP). Kabul denies it.
A TTP ambush on 11 November killed at least 10 police, officials told AP.
why_it_matters: Fighting between Pakistan and the Taliban government risks civilian deaths and wider instability. Pakistan has struck alleged TTP hideouts in Afghanistan, AP notes.
verify_note: Each side blames the other for starting the clashes. Local sources told Afghan media, as reported by Long War Journal, that Pakistan started the 29 October fighting; Dawn links the 1 November clash to an Afghan check post.

sources.title: Taliban-Pakistan border clashes continue, TTP attack kills 10 Pakistani police
sources.supports: Dated account of border clashes on 29 October and 1 November, the Torkham crossing closing for five hours, and the 11 November TTP ambush. Local sources said Pakistani forces started the 29 October fighting.

sources.title: Pakistan warns Afghanistan of 'unbearable punishment' as clashes persist along border
sources.supports: The Torkham crossing closed for nearly five hours on 1 November and a civilian was killed by a mortar near Angoor Adda. Pakistan's military blames the Taliban for sheltering the TTP. Dawn links the clash to an Afghan check post.

sources.title: Militants ambush police in Pakistan, sparking gunbattle that kills 10 officers and 18 militants
sources.supports: Militants ambushed police on 11 November; officials say at least 10 police and 18 militants died. The TTP claimed it. Kabul denies sheltering the group.

title: China reports patrols at Scarborough Shoal
summary: China's southern military command says it held readiness patrols at the shoal on 30 October.
The Philippines is tracking a Chinese vessel with unidentified equipment inside the lagoon.
Analysts told Radio Free Asia both sides appear to be lowering tension as the ASEAN and APEC summits open.
why_it_matters: The shoal is a flashpoint between China and a US treaty ally. Manila says it lies inside its exclusive economic zone.
verify_note: Each detail rests on one outlet, and none is a wire service: The Defense Post (patrols, vessel), Radio Free Asia (calming) and CSIS AMTI (July data). China's claims could not be independently checked. No clash in November was found.

sources.title: Philippine Coast Guard Probes Chinese Vessel With Unidentified Equipment Inside Scarborough Shoal
sources.supports: Philippine coast guard is probing a Chinese vessel in the lagoon; China's Southern Theater Command says it held readiness patrols on 30 October as a countermeasure.

sources.title: Filipino fishermen urge Manila to defend territorial waters - their fishing grounds
sources.supports: The Philippines hosts the ASEAN summit 15 to 17 November hoping to finalise a code of conduct; analysts doubt it; both sides seem to be lowering tensions.

sources.title: Occupational Risk? Chinese Presence Surges at Scarborough Shoal
sources.supports: China Coast Guard patrols at the shoal totalled 933 ship-days in the first half of 2026, nearly the 1,099 for all of 2025.

title: North Korea tests missiles as talks stay uncertain
summary: North Korea said it tested a strategic cruise missile with a dispersal warhead on 2 November, and an air-defence missile on 4 November.
South Korea's military says several missiles flew toward the East Sea on 4 November.
President Trump may seek another meeting with Kim Jong Un, but no talks are announced.
why_it_matters: Frequent tests continue while diplomacy with Washington and Seoul remains stuck. North Korea says the tests show new weapons technology.
verify_note: All reports rely on KCNA and South Korea's military. Only Stars and Stripes (5 November) carries a US crypto-theft finding, which North Korea disputes; it is not used. No tests found after 5 November.

sources.title: North Korea claims new missile technology as Trump-Kim diplomacy remains in doubt
sources.supports: KCNA says a new air-defence system was tested on 4 November; South Korea saw missiles launched from Sondok; speculation about a Trump-Kim meeting, but no talks announced.

sources.title: N. Korea says it test-fired new air defense missile system
sources.supports: South Korea's Joint Chiefs say missiles flew under 300 km toward the East Sea; a cruise missile unit also ran a strike drill on a simulated airport target.

sources.title: North Korea claims cruise missile warhead can devastate 15-acre area
sources.supports: KCNA says North Korea tested a strategic cruise missile with a dispersal warhead on 2 November.

title: Japan-China row heads to APEC summit
summary: Relations are at one of their lowest points since 1972, after a Taiwan remark by Japan's prime minister Takaichi last year.
China has warned its citizens against travel to Japan and, per Bloomberg, curbed seafood imports and rare earth exports.
Takaichi may get only a brief handshake from Xi at the APEC summit in Shenzhen this week. Kyodo says no sit-down is planned.
why_it_matters: Two of Asia's largest economies are in a long dispute linked to Taiwan, which affects trade and regional security.
verify_note: AFP (via France 24), Bloomberg (via The Star), Reuters and Jiji Press opened. Only Bloomberg names the seafood and rare earth measures. Whether a meeting happens is not yet known.

sources.title: Frosty China welcome likely for Japan PM due to Taiwan row
sources.supports: Takaichi expected to get a brief handshake from Xi; Beijing now asks for a correction of her remark, softer than a retraction; Kyodo says no sit-down is planned.

sources.title: Japan works to shield Takaichi from any Xi snub at China's APEC summit
sources.supports: Bloomberg says ties are near their lowest since 1972 and China limited rare earth exports and seafood to Japan; Takaichi has not retracted her remark.

sources.title: Taiwan says China is conducting 'area denial' drills in Western Pacific
sources.supports: The APEC summit is in Shenzhen next week.

sources.title: Japan-China summit faces uncertainty ahead of APEC meeting
sources.supports: Takaichi made the Taiwan remarks on 7 November 2025 in the Diet. China hosts the APEC leaders' summit in Shenzhen on 18 to 19 November 2026. A Takaichi-Xi summit is uncertain.

title: Sudan's army says it is pushing RSF back in Kordofan
summary: Sudan's army and the paramilitary RSF have fought since April 2023. The RSF holds almost all of Darfur.
The army says it retook Al-Khuway in West Kordofan on 13 November. The RSF has not confirmed this.
US-led efforts for a 90-day humanitarian truce had not succeeded by early August.
why_it_matters: Millions are displaced, and a UN-backed hunger monitor said in May that 14 areas were at risk of famine.
verify_note: The 13 November Al-Khuway claim rests on Radio Tamazuj and comes from the army side; the RSF could not be reached. Outside backing of the RSF is disputed: the UAE denies supporting it.

sources.title: Sudanese army, allies announce recapture of key West Kordofan town
sources.supports: Army and allied Joint Force say they retook Al-Khuway on 13 November after heavy fighting; the RSF could not be reached and the claims were not independently verified.

sources.title: Is the Sudanese army gaining momentum against the RSF?
sources.supports: Describes front lines: army holds Khartoum, north, east and centre; RSF holds most of the west. About 14 million displaced. Says the war is far from settled.

sources.title: U.S.-brokered peace efforts for Sudan encounter new obstacles
sources.supports: US adviser Massad Boulos is trying to revive a 90-day truce. The army demands RSF withdrawal from cities first. The RSF calls that surrender.

sources.title: UK's Yvette Cooper denies UAE sent British arms to Sudan's RSF with more than a 'dozen countries' fuelling war
sources.supports: UK says over a dozen countries feed arms flows to both sides. Sudan's army-backed prime minister points to UAE support for the RSF. The UAE has repeatedly denied this.

title: Ethiopia and Eritrea accuse each other of starting a war
summary: A TPLF-led rebel alliance attacked in northern Ethiopia on 23 September, then left Mekelle on 3 October.
Eritrea cut ties on 1 October. A mid-October rebel counteroffensive hit federal supply lines, Addis Standard says.
Ethiopia says Eritrean troops entered Tigray. Eritrea denies it and says it faces aggression.
why_it_matters: An analyst told Al Jazeera it is the most dangerous moment between the two states since the 1998 to 2000 war, with a risk of links to the Sudan war.
verify_note: Eritrean troop movements are alleged by Ethiopia and reported by witnesses, not independently verified. The latest firm battlefield detail found dates from October.

sources.title: Ethiopia and Eritrea accuse one another of launching war
sources.supports: Ethiopia told the UN Eritrean troops advanced up to 60 km into Tigray. Eritrea calls itself the target. Ties collapsed and the federal army took Mekelle.

sources.title: Ethiopia, Eritrea break ties: Does the conflict risk becoming regional war?
sources.supports: Eritrea cut ties on 1 October. Fighting in Tigray, Amhara and Afar is the worst since 2020-2022. Analysts fear spread to Sudan and Egypt.

sources.title: Ethiopia's Second Tigray War - Same Battlefield, Different Political Reality
sources.supports: Federal forces and Tigrayan allies hold Mekelle. The TPLF says it will keep fighting. Ethiopia's talk of the Assab port alarms Eritrea. This is an analyst commentary.

sources.title: Ethiopia, Eritrea ramp up rhetoric: Are they inching towards war?
sources.supports: Ethiopia cited the UN self-defence article. ACLED reported Eritrean troops near Zalambessa hit by Ethiopian drones. Analysts call it the most dangerous moment since 1998-2000.

title: US and China extend trade truce again
summary: A one-year trade truce from October 2025 was due to end on 10 November.
China extended its pause on some critical mineral export controls to 10 January 2027.
The US extended 178 tariff exclusions, The National reports. Bessent urged China in early November to meet its commitments in full.
why_it_matters: The two largest economies control tariffs and rare earth supplies that affect factories and prices worldwide.
verify_note: No outcome of the Trump-Xi meeting at APEC was reported by 17 November. The tariff details rest on The National; Reuters confirms the 10 January date.

sources.title: China extends pause on rare earth export curbs for two months
sources.supports: China's commerce ministry extended the truce to 10 January and suspended a 24% tariff. The US extended 178 exclusions. Bessent wants full compliance. Trump and Xi expected to meet next week.

sources.title: US, China agree to extend trade truce by two months, work on bigger deal, Bessent says
sources.supports: Bessent said the sides agreed a two-month extension and are exploring a bigger deal. He said China lags on some farm purchases and rare earth deliveries.

sources.title: China extends suspension of rare earth export controls until January
sources.supports: China's commerce ministry extended the suspension of some export controls for two months, to 10 January 2027.

title: Jihadists and rebels press Mali's military junta
summary: In April, al-Qaeda-linked JNIM and Tuareg separatists (FLA) attacked army sites across Mali.
Mali's army says it retook Kidal on 6 October with Russian help. The FLA says it left by choice.
JNIM claimed a September attack on the Dioura army camp. AFP sources said at least 50 soldiers died.
why_it_matters: ACLED counts about 3,400 deaths from militant attacks in Mali in the first seven months of 2026, and AP says JNIM is expanding towards coastal West Africa.
verify_note: The Kidal account rests on Al Jazeera, which reports the army claim and the FLA statement. No wire-service report from November was found. A 2 November attack rests only on a JNIM claim and is not used.

sources.title: Mali's army says it has taken Kidal from Tuareg rebels, with Russia's help
sources.supports: Army says it retook Kidal with Russia's Africa Corps. The FLA calls it a controlled withdrawal. An analyst calls it symbolic, not decisive.

sources.title: What to know about the conflict in Mali and the world's most terrorized region
sources.supports: JNIM and FLA joined forces in April. ACLED shows deaths up 35% in 2026. Russia's Africa Corps fights beside the army. JNIM is expanding towards coastal states.

sources.title: Al Qaeda-linked militants curb their brutality in seized Malian territory
sources.supports: JNIM attacked Bamako's airport in April. Mali's government refuses talks. In areas JNIM holds, residents report softer rule. JNIM still carries out deadly attacks.

sources.title: At least 50 soldiers killed in jihadist attack on Malian army base
sources.supports: JNIM claimed control of the Dioura army camp in Mopti region; security and local sources told AFP at least 50 soldiers and five Africa Corps fighters died.

title: US steers Venezuela's post-Maduro transition and oil
summary: US forces captured President Maduro on 3 January 2026, AP reported. Delcy Rodriguez later became acting president.
On 2 November Rubio met Venezuela's foreign minister and restated a three-phase plan ending in elections.
Under oil deals this year, the Pentagon holds 35% of a joint-venture operating company. Opposition leader Machado criticises it.
why_it_matters: Washington now shapes Venezuela's politics and oil, which affects the region and fuel prices.
verify_note: A partisan outlet claimed new US strikes in November; no credible source confirmed this, so it is not used. Trump's claims about oil shipments were not confirmed.

sources.title: US urges Venezuela to follow phased plan for democratic transition
sources.supports: Rubio met Foreign Minister Blanco on 2 November. The US plan has three phases. Rodriguez gave no election date. Details of the oil joint venture.

sources.title: Rubio meets Venezuelan counterpart as US presses for progress on election preparations
sources.supports: Rubio urged release of remaining political prisoners. Venezuelan authorities and opposition agreed a reform blueprint with elections targeted for 2027. Bessent backed energy production.

sources.title: Trump touts Venezuelan oil at Texas rally ahead of US midterms
sources.supports: Trump pointed to a tanker he said held 1 million barrels of Venezuelan oil. Pentagon holds a 35% stake in the oil venture. Details of the shipment were unclear.

sources.title: US-Venezuela news LIVE: Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro captured, with wife Cilia Flores, amid US strikes, Donald Trump says
sources.supports: AP live report, 3 January 2026: US forces captured President Nicolas Maduro and his wife amid US strikes.
